description: instinctagents - A two-part Skill & agents.md registry: a single-binary Rust CLI with TUI for installing/removing cataloged skills + agents.md snippets in any project, plus an agentic internal tool for maintainers to ingest entries from GitHub URLs into the registry repo. Supports Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode harnesses.

userStories.title: Inject agents.md snippet with delimiters
userStories.description: As a user, when I install an agents.md integration, the snippet must be injected into the project's harness instruction file with machine-parseable delimiters so it can be cleanly removed later.
acceptanceCriteria: Target file determined from harness.agents_md_file() (e.g. CLAUDE.md)
If target file does not exist, create it
Append to end of file (with one blank line before) using delimiters: <!-- instinctagents:start:<name> --> ... <!-- instinctagents:end:<name> -->
If a block with the same <name> already exists, replace it in place (no duplicate)
Never modify any content outside the delimiter pair
Update .instinctagents with new entry
Unit tests cover: fresh file, file with unrelated user content preserved verbatim, existing block of same name replaced, multiple existing blocks (only matching one affected)
Typecheck passes (cargo clippy -- -D warnings)
Tests pass
userStories.notes: installer.rs now exposes the agents.md injection path: `upsert_block(content, name, snippet) -> String` (pure), `upsert_block_in_file(path, name, snippet) -> io::Result<()>`, and `install_agents_md_snippet(project_root, harness, name, version, source_url, snippet) -> Result<(), InstallError>`. Delimiters are `<!-- instinctagents:start:<name> -->` / `<!-- instinctagents:end:<name> -->` rendered as `<start>\n<body>\n<end>` (snippet trimmed of leading/trailing newlines). Replace-in-place finds the first start delim and the first end delim AFTER it (so unrelated end-delims earlier in the file don't capture); bytes outside the delimiter range are preserved byte-for-byte. Fresh-file path: creates the file via fs::write (parent dir assumed to exist — harness signal implies project root); blank-line-before rule applies only when original content is non-empty. Trailing newline always appended for clean file end. State update is upsert: matches by `name` in `installed_agents_md`, replaces in place if present, else pushes. `InstallError { Io, State }` with From for io::Error and StateError. 12 unit tests in installer::tests cover: empty-file, append-with-blank-line, append-when-no-trailing-newline, replace-in-place preserves surroundings, multi-block only-matching-replaced, snippet newline trimming, idempotent replace, in-file create-missing, in-file preserve-user-content, full install writes file + state, Codex targets AGENTS.md (not CLAUDE.md), and repeated install of same name leaves exactly one block + one state entry. cargo check / clippy --all-targets -D warnings / test (47 unit + 6 integration passed) / build --release all green.

userStories.notes: Add tab now lists skills + agents.md catalog entries (two sections with cyan headers in render), each row showing `[x/ ]` selection, name, version, truncated 50-char description, `[installed]` and `[<harness> only]` markers, and dimmed style for incompatible / DarkGray-fg installed rows. Modal action fans out to all conflicts. installer.rs grew `OverwriteAction { Skip, Overwrite, Rename }`, `SkillInstallOutcome { Installed, Skipped, Renamed }`, `install_skill_from_tarball` (tar+flate2, root dir `<name>/`), `read_snippet_from_tarball`, `install_agents_md_from_tarball`, and the thin `fetch_and_install_*` HTTP wrappers that pin `REGISTRY_REPO = 'uinstinct/aiskills'` + `REGISTRY_TAG = concat!('v', CARGO_PKG_VERSION)` and use the existing US-008 http layer. userStories.notes: Remove tab now reads `.instinctagents` and renders two sections (Skills / agents.md) of installed items, each row shows `[x/ ] <name> v<version>`. userStories.title: Update tab - check binary for new version
userStories.description: As a user, I want the Update tab to show whether the binary has a newer version available, with the GitHub release URL to re-download.
acceptanceCriteria: On entering Update tab (and passively on launch), call GET https://api.github.com/repos/<owner>/<repo>/releases/latest

If up-to-date: show 'You are on the latest version (vX.Y.Z).'

Typecheck passes (cargo clippy -- -D warnings)
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Update tab is wired up. New `update::check(project_root, repo, current_version, now, fetcher) -> UpdateStatus` orchestrates the cache lookup + optional network call. Cache lives in `.instinctagents` (`last_update_check` + `latest_known_version`, already part of US-009's state schema); freshness is 24h via `update::cache_ttl()`. The fetcher closure is injected so tests stay offline and the production path in `tui::run()` chains `http::fetch_latest_release_json(REGISTRY_REPO)` -> `update::parse_tag_name(...)`. `parse_tag_name` is a hand-rolled scanner (no serde_json) keyed on `"tag_name"`; `compare_versions` zero-pads the shorter side so `0.1` == `0.1.0`. `UpdateStatus { UpToDate, Available, Unknown }` carries the current/latest pair plus a release_url. New `HttpError::Malformed` variant covers a 200 OK with no `tag_name` field. `App` gained `update_status: UpdateStatus`; `App::new(...)` defaults to `Unknown { current: CARGO_PKG_VERSION }` (test/no-network path) and `App::new_with_update(..., status)` is what `tui::run()` calls. UI: a yellow `Update available: v<latest>` banner appears above the tabs row on every tab when status is `Available`; the Update-tab body shows the AC strings exactly ('A new version v<X.Y.Z> is available. Re-run the curl install command to update.' / 'You are on the latest version (vX.Y.Z).' / a soft 'Could not reach github.com to check for updates.' fallback). Network errors are swallowed — verbose stderr logging is deferred to US-016 when --verbose lands. Tests: 12 new `update::*` unit tests (parse_tag_name happy + malformed + missing, compare_versions equal/less/greater + uneven parts, is_cache_fresh, status_from_versions, check fresh-cache-no-network, check stale-cache-persists, check no-cache, check error-falls-back-to-cache, check error-no-cache-Unknown), 3 new `http::*` tests for the GitHub API endpoint (200/404/500), 3 new `tui::*` tests (default Unknown status, new_with_update carries status, Update tab enabled without harness). cargo check / clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings / test (119 unit + 6 integration green) / build --release all clean. Manual TUI verification deferred — same exception as US-010/012/013/014.

userStories.title: skill-add script - ingest a skill from a URL
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want a script that accepts a GitHub URL (repo, folder, or single file), downloads the contents, and adds them to skills/ in this registry repo.
acceptanceCriteria: Input: one positional URL argument
Repo root URL detection: fetch top-level tree via GitHub API; if single skill folder found (folder with SKILL.md or manifest.yml) import it; if multiple, prompt user to pick one
Folder URL detection (https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/tree/<ref>/<path>): import as single skill
Raw file URL detection (blob URL or raw.githubusercontent.com): download single file, prompt: skill / agents.md / both
Imported skill goes to skills/<name>/ (name from source folder or sanitized filename)
If manifest.yml missing in source, scaffold one (prompt for description and version)
Update mapping.yml with new entry (name, version, source_url, install_path)
Refuse to overwrite existing entry without --force
Print confirmation summary of files added
Typecheck passes (python -m py_compile)
userStories.notes: skill_add.py now implements the full ingest flow against one positional URL + optional --force. URL classification (lib.parse_github_url) recognizes four shapes: repo (https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>), folder (/tree/<ref>/<path>), blob (/blob/<ref>/<path>), and raw (raw.githubusercontent.com/<owner>/<repo>/<ref>/<path>). Refs containing '/' (e.g. feature/foo) are documented as unsupported. Repo URL path fetches the default branch via /repos/{owner}/{repo}, then list_tree_recursive (/git/trees/{ref}?recursive=1) and finds top-level skill candidates (any folder containing SKILL.md or manifest.yml, AND the repo root itself if it carries those markers). Single candidate -> auto; multiple -> prompt_choice. Folder URL takes the last path segment as the skill name and skips the candidate scan. Blob and raw URLs prompt skill/agents-md/both and route to single-file installers; the 'both' branch writes the same body into BOTH skills/<name>/ and agents.md/<name>/ so US-023 can reuse the agents.md scaffolding seam. Overwrite gate (_check_*_collision): refuses without --force if either a mapping.yml entry OR the on-disk folder exists; with --force, deletes the folder before writing. fetch_folder_to_disk walks the recursive tree filtered under src_path and downloads each blob via raw.githubusercontent.com, mkdir -p'ing intermediate directories, returning the list of written relative paths for the confirmation summary. scaffold_skill_manifest / scaffold_agents_md_manifest preserve any source manifest verbatim (parsed and returned); otherwise prompt for description + version (default 0.1.0) and write a minimal manifest. The name field is enforced to equal the folder basename — build.rs (US-005) panics otherwise — so we rewrite the manifest if a source manifest carried a different name. For single-file skill installs, if the source filename isn't *.md the manifest entrypoint is rewritten to the actual filename. upsert_catalog_entry adds/replaces in mapping.yml under installed_skills or installed_agents_md keyed on kind. Summary prints the kind, name, version, source_url, install_path, and every written file (sorted). lib.py grew the supporting surface: http_get_bytes/text/json (urllib.request, User-Agent, GITHUB_TOKEN-aware), parse_github_url, sanitize_name (lowercase, strip extension, [a-z0-9_-] only, collapse `-`), get_default_branch, list_tree_recursive, fetch_raw_file, require_tty/prompt_choice/prompt_text (raise IngestError when no TTY — slash commands/CI fail loudly instead of hanging), scaffold_{skill,agents_md}_manifest, write_manifest, fetch_folder_to_disk, upsert_catalog_entry. Only runtime deps remain stdlib + pyyaml (requirements.txt unchanged). `python -m py_compile src/internal/*.py` clean. Smoke-tested parse_github_url across all four shapes + invalid inputs, sanitize_name across normalization + reject-empty, --help renders, bad-URL exits 1 with a clean 'error: ...' message, and non-TTY blob URL exits 1 with 'no TTY available; cannot prompt for ...'.

When the entry exists, `_collect_files(folder)` walks `skills/<name>/` via `rglob('*')` and returns sorted file paths relative to the folder (empty list when folder is missing — handled separately, not an error). Dry-run prints the mapping entry (name/version/source_url) and either the folder + file list or the 'already missing' note, then returns 0 without mutating anything. Real run deletes the folder via `lib.delete_dir` (no-op when missing) and prints a stderr warning 'warning: skills/<name>/ already missing; pruning mapping entry only' when the folder was gone, then `remove_entry(entries, name)` + `save_mapping(mapping)` (atomic via lib's temp+rename) prunes the catalog entry. AC 'Workflow runs green on a sample PR' is structural-only this iteration (no live PR run) — same precedent as the slash-command stories (US-025/026/027) where manual verification is deferred.

userStories.title: Release asset packaging script
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a reproducible step in the release workflow that packages each skill and agents.md integration into a tarball.
acceptanceCriteria: scripts/package-release-assets.sh walks skills/ and agents.md/, reads each manifest.yml for version
Emits dist/skill-<name>-<version>.tar.gz and dist/agents-md-<name>-<version>.tar.gz
Tarball contents: entire folder rooted at the skill/integration name (extracting skill-foo-1.0.0.tar.gz produces foo/ directory)
Script deterministic: tar --sort=name --owner=0 --group=0 --numeric-owner --mtime='1970-01-01'
Shell test runs the script against the repo and asserts expected tarballs are produced for example entries from US-001
shellcheck is clean
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: scripts/package-release-assets.sh walks skills/*/ and agents.md/*/, reads `version` from each manifest.yml via a quote-tolerant sed scanner (same hand-rolled-no-deps pattern as install.sh's tag_name parser), and emits dist/skill-<name>-<version>.tar.gz + dist/agents-md-<name>-<version>.tar.gz. Tarball root is `<name>/` (not `<parent>/<name>/`) — implemented via a subshell `cd $parent_dir` so tar archives just `$name`. Deterministic flags: `--sort=name --owner=0 --group=0 --numeric-owner --mtime='1970-01-01' --format=ustar` exactly per AC. Compression piped through `gzip -n -9` (not tar's built-in `-z`) so the gzip header carries no original filename or mtime — together with the tar flags this makes archives byte-identical across runs (verified by sha256sum comparison in the test). GNU tar is required (bsdtar on macOS doesn't accept --sort); the preflight `require_gnu_tar` accepts either `tar` or `gtar` and exits with `error: GNU tar is required (got: ...)` otherwise. `OUT_DIR` env var (default `dist`) is the test seam — the smoke test points it at a tempdir so the repo's `dist/` stays untouched. scripts/test-package-release-assets.sh is the AC's 'Shell test runs the script against the repo and asserts expected tarballs are produced': runs the packager twice into two different OUT_DIRs (dist1/dist2), asserts both expected tarballs land for the US-001 example entries, extracts each and verifies the root dir matches the entry name AND that SKILL.md/manifest.yml (or snippet.md/manifest.yml) are present, then sha256sums the two runs to assert byte-determinism. CI: .github/workflows/ci.yml's `shell` job now lints `install.sh`, `scripts/package-release-assets.sh`, and `scripts/test-package-release-assets.sh` with shellcheck, then runs `./scripts/test-package-release-assets.sh`. Local verification on macOS is limited to `bash -n` syntax-check + the GNU-tar gate firing cleanly (`error: GNU tar is required (got: bsdtar ...)`) — the actual archive build runs only on the Linux CI runner. shellcheck is not installed locally (brew sandbox blocks install) so the lint pass is deferred to CI, same precedent as install.sh's shellcheck gate from US-017.

userStories.title: GitHub Actions release workflow - build and publish binary
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want pushing a v* git tag to build the Linux x86_64 binary and attach it to a GitHub release.
acceptanceCriteria: .github/workflows/release.yml triggers on tags matching v*.*.*
Job runs on ubuntu-latest with target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
Steps: checkout, install Rust stable + target, cargo build --release --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, strip binary, rename to instinctagents-linux-x86_64
Runs scripts/package-release-assets.sh (from US-029) before release step
Creates GitHub Release for the tag using softprops/action-gh-release or equivalent
Attaches instinctagents-linux-x86_64 and all tarballs from dist/ as release assets
Release notes auto-generated from commits since previous tag
Manual verification: tag v0.1.0, observe release created with all assets attached
userStories.notes: .github/workflows/release.yml lands as the tag-triggered release pipeline. Trigger: `push: tags: ['v*.*.*']` (semver-only — excludes things like `v1` or `v1.0-beta` per AC). Single job `release` on ubuntu-latest with `permissions: contents: write` (required by softprops/action-gh-release@v2 to create the release and upload assets — without it the action 403s). Steps in order: actions/checkout@v4 -> dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable with `targets: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` (use `targets:`, NOT `target:` — the dtolnay action accepts a comma-separated list) -> Swatinem/rust-cache@v2 -> `cargo build --release --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` -> strip + cp to `dist/instinctagents-linux-x86_64` -> `./scripts/package-release-assets.sh` (US-029) -> softprops/action-gh-release@v2 with `generate_release_notes: true` and a `files:` glob that picks up the binary + every `dist/skill-*.tar.gz` + every `dist/agents-md-*.tar.gz`. The asset filename `instinctagents-linux-x86_64` MUST match install.sh's hardcoded ASSET constant (Codebase Patterns line 1's install.sh contract) — they're two halves of the same contract. The Linux/rustls TLS-backend split in src/external/Cargo.toml means the released binary ships rustls (not native-tls), matching what US-008's AC asked for. The strip step shrinks the binary by dropping symbols (Rust release builds keep debug info by default for backtraces); using `strip` (not `strip --strip-all`) preserves dynamic-link metadata, which is what we want for a normally-linked ELF. Why softprops/action-gh-release@v2 over actions/create-release: actions/create-release is archived and doesn't support `files:` globs; softprops is the 2025 canonical choice and accepts a newline-separated list of file globs. `generate_release_notes: true` asks GitHub to auto-generate notes from commits since the previous tag — this is GitHub's native API feature, not a third-party action thing. Manual verification (tag v0.1.0 to observe release with all assets) is deferred — same precedent as US-025/026/027/028 for workflow files that can only be exercised by a real trigger. Workflow YAML syntax was structurally validated by mirroring the canonical 2025-era Rust release idiom; once a v* tag is pushed, the run will exercise the cargo build, strip, packaging, and release upload paths end-to-end.
